## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Ekarājacariya* ("The Conduct of the One King") is a text in the *Cariyāpiṭaka* collection of the Pali canon. In this narrative, the Bodhisatta is depicted in a past life as the renowned monarch Ekarājā, who firmly undertakes and resolutely determines upon supreme morality (*paramaṁ sīlaṁ adhiṭṭhāya*) [Lim 2009]. Valuing omniscience above all else, he establishes his firm resolve, proclaiming in the concluding verses that no one equalled him in resolute determination (*adhiṭṭhānapāramī*) [Lim 2009].

In scholarly discussion of early Buddhist doctrine, the text serves as a key exemplar of the perfection of resolute determination (*adhiṭṭhāna*) and moral resolve [Lim 2009].
